8-280A. Military Occupational Specialty 280A – Software Operations Technician (Effective
202507)
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. NA.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21.
   c. MOS 280A. MOS 280A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is any MOS.
   Candidates must possess the following qualifications.
        (a) Must be SGT (E-5) or Above
        (b) Must have completed Warrior Leaders Course (WLC)
        (b) Must meet all Administrative Requirements to become a Warrant Officer.
                   • Including be a U.S. citizen (No waivers)
                   • Possess a SECRET with eligibility to obtain TOP SECRET (No waivers)
                   • ASVAB GT Score of 110 (No waivers)
                   • High-School Graduate or GED (No waivers)
                   • Pass Commissioning Physical
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI.
        5J--Software Development Engineer
        5L--Platform Engineer
        5M--Technical Mission Force Cadre
       Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant officer
       MOS)).
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) All applicants must apply, be accepted, and graduate from the Army Software Factory
280A Software Development Engineer Training Program. Complete the Software Factory Paired
Industry Partner program and complete the one-year utilization program within the Army Software
Factory.
        (2) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Be a U.S. citizen. Possess a TOP SECRET security clearance with eligibility for
access to sensitive compartmented information (SCI).
              (b) Complete 280A Software Operations Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course.
              (c) Possess a 280A Software Operations Additional Skill Identifier (ASI)
                    • 5J--Software Development Engineer
                    • 5L--Platform Engineer
              (d) Upon completion of 280A Software Operations Technician Warrant Officer Basic
Course, WOs incur a 6-year term of service obligation.
        (3) CW3 must—
                   (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (2).
                   (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Advanced Common Core.
                   (c) Complete 280A Software Operations Technician Warrant Officer Advanced
Course.
        (4) CW4 must—
                   (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (3).
                   (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
        (5) CW5 must—
                   (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (4).
                   (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
g. Duties.
   (1) WO1/CW2 must-
       (a) A Basic-level Software Operations Technician leverages fundamentals of software
development using basic programming language features, fundamental cybersecurity and secure
 software development concepts, Product Management, standard software architecture, software
development engineering practices, platform engineering practices, and employing scripting
languages at an intermediate level.
        (b) A Basic-level Software Operations Technician – Software Development Engineer has a
basic-level understanding of the software development discipline, common data structures and
algorithms, basic software architecture patterns, prototyping, object-oriented and functional
programming, secure software development principles, and database architecture and design.
Includes modules of Software Development Core Competencies, Cyber Security Fundamentals,
Micro Service Applications, and Containerization Fundamentals. Responsible for full-stack web
application development, low-code/no-code application development, digital-system plug-ins, and
common operating picture plug-ins.
        (c) A Basic-level Software Operations Technician – Platform Engineer understands the
foundational concepts involved with software and platform development disciplines with an
emphasis on infrastructure, application hosting, and container orchestration. Includes modules of
Platform Development Operations Core Competencies, Cyber Security Fundamentals.
Administers platform applications for software development teams to develop, deploy, and scale
their applications.
        (d) Complete assigned tasks and modules, as required and assigned by a Senior- or
Master-level Software Operations Technician.
      (2) CW3 must--
        (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (1).
        (b) A Senior-level Software Operations Technician leverages Lean and Agile
methodologies and management practices to lead software development and platform
engineering teams through the creation and management of software and platform projects.
        (c) A Senior-level Software Operations Technician must have senior-level expertise within
a specialized focus area and possess a deep understanding of the product development lifecycle
and DevSecOps. Collaborates with and advises adjacent software operations specialties on
technical direction, risk mitigation, and impacts to a project’s overall engineering efforts.
Propagates a deep understanding of testing methodologies and code/infrastructure development.
Consolidates operational lessons learned from subordinate echelons and informs Master-level
engineers of unique challenges or project impediments. Integrates new practices or technologies
into current operations. Also provides training, guidance, oversight, and direction to Basic-level
Software Operations Technicians working under their tutelage. Provides mentorship and talent
management for career progression of Junior Warrant Officers. Responsible for decomposing
projects into components which can be assigned to Basic-level Software Operations Technicians.
        (d) A Senior-level Software Operations Technician – Software Development Engineer
serves on a cross-functional team leveraging an advanced-level of understanding of
programming language features, software architecture design patterns, and programming
concepts to build cloud-native and mobile applications or plugins. Develops and facilitates training
pathways for Junior Software Development Engineers. Enforces industry best practices, such as
secure software development, pair-programming, and test-driven development standards across
the organization.
        (e) A Senior-level Software Operations Technician – Platform Engineer understands and
employs the software and platform development disciplines with an emphasis on infrastructure,
application hosting, and container orchestration. Includes modules of Platform Development
Operations Advanced Competencies, Cyber Security Best Practices, Containerization
Operations, and managing a Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) Pipeline.
Develops and maintains application teams’ path to production, services, tooling, and DevSecOps
platform. Leverages platform engineering principles to host cloud-native applications for software
development teams to develop, deploy, and scale their applications. Enforces industry best
practices and standards across the organization.
        (f) A Senior-level Software Operations Technician is responsible for completing assigned
tasks and modules, as required and assigned by a Master-level Software Operations Technician.
    (3) CW4 must--
        (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (2).
          (b) A Master-level Software Operations Technician possesses skills in negotiation, policy
analysis, and development. Can demonstrate knowledge in force management and emerging
technologies.
         (c) Serve as a principal advisor to decision and policy makers on Software Operations
training, policies, and procedures in areas of software development, platform engineering, and
security principles. Responsible for collaborating on operational and strategic-level solutions.
         (d) Must have Master-level expertise within a specialized focus area and is responsible for
advising, aligning, and directing organizational technical infrastructure. Informs design patterns,
technologies, and practices that achieve organizational outcomes while reinforcing training career
progression opportunities for software operations cross-functional teams.
         (e) Set conditions for intermediate and senior level Software Operations Technicians to
mentor more junior level Software Operations Technicians in product development lifecycle and
DevSecOps.
         (f) Mentor Senior-level Software Operations Technician as they progress to the Master
level.
    (4) CW5 must--
         (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (3).
         (b) Deliver master-level technical and tactical expertise on the primary duties of technical
leader, manager, multidiscipline Software Operations integrator, and advisor.
         (c) Provide direction, guidance, resources, assistance, and supervision necessary for
subordinates to perform their duties.
         (d) Support commanders with the development of new Software Operations doctrine,
organizational structure, methods and equipment to be utilized by Software Operations
Technicians.
         (e) Provide leader development, talent and lifecycle management, mentorship, advice, and
counsel to enlisted Soldiers, warrant officers, and branch officers.
         (f) Possess special leadership abilities that interprets the commander’s intent and mission
to support Multi-Domain Operations (MDO), representing and advising on the responsibilities of
Software Operations within their respective AOR.
         (g) Primarily support corps, echelons above corps, major command, Joint, Interagency,
Intergovernmental, and Multinational operations.
h. Physical demands category, grading, and position titles.
    (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderately Heavy.
    (2) Meet physical standards per AR 40-501, chapter 2.
    (3) Have 20/40 correctable vision per AR 40-501, paragraphs 2-13 and 5-17 and meet hearing
standards of AR 40-501, paragraphs 2-7 and 5-18.
    (4) Table 8-280A-1. Physical requirements.
    (a) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT)
– 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles
Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
     (5) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2
equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables: Table 8-280A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
